topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: Where Infinite Sums Behave Differently
target_audience: Undergraduate mathematics students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Usual Notion of Convergence
lecture_lines: A series is the limit of partial sums.
Geometric series converge on a number line.
animations: Display a sequence labeled 'S_n' on screen in white (#FFFFFF) alongside.
Highlight the final terms of S_n as they approach limit L in blue (#0000FF).
Draw an arrow representing |S_n - L| shrinking to zero in green (#00FF00).

sections.title: Introducing the 2-adic Metric
lecture_lines: High powers of 2 are very small.
animations: Display '2^n' with n as a variable exponent in yellow (#FFFF00).
Flash the exponent n and show |2^n|_2 = 1/2^n in magenta (#FF00FF).
Scale a shrinking rectangle down as n increases to visualize smallness in cyan (#00FFFF) while measuring the reduction using.

sections.title: Infinite Sums in 2-adic Space
animations: Display terms 1, 2, 4, 8 as powers of 2 in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate each term shifting to the right indicating higher divisibility in light blue (#ADD8E6).
Show partial sums S_k approaching -1 in red (#FF0000).

sections.title: The Ultrametric Inequality (The 'No-Overlap' Rule)
lecture_lines: The ultrametric inequality forbids standard stretching.
Distances do not add up normally.
animations: Show two concentric representing balls in 2-adic space in purple (#800080).
Animate a contained within another to illustrate ultrametric rule in orange (#FFA500).
Display the formula |x+y| <= max(|x|, |y|) with labels in lime (#32CD32).

sections.title: Application and Summary
lecture_lines: Infinite series can be contained integers.
animations: Summarize core concepts: 2-adic norm and series convergence in white (#FFFFFF) using.
Display a 2-adic calculation result: 1+2+4+... = -1 in yellow (#FFFF00) using.
Fade all visualized elements smoothly to black (#000000).
